entradas.text: I'd had the chef prepare barbecued ribs for the occasion. I hoped they were still his favorite.
Nearly half an hour after he said he'd be there, Franc burst through the door.
"You're late."
entradas.menu: "You're late."

entradas.text: "Is everything all right?"
entradas.menu: "Is everything all right?"

entradas.text: "Yeah, I know. I'm sorry."
"Yeah, yeah. I'm sorry."
"Are some of those guards outside new? I had to convince them I was really your son."
"I ran into a couple of my friends protesting outside your gates. It was pretty awkward, telling them I was having dinner with you."
"They might be."
entradas.menu: "They might be."

entradas.text: "I'm starting to get suspicious of them, to be honest."
entradas.menu: "I'm starting to get suspicious of them, to be honest."

entradas.text: "Well, I'd be more suspicious of them if I were you."
He flung his backpack on the living room sofa and sprawled out in a chair.
"Shit, Dad, that parade was a close call. I thought the ball was bad..."
"Serge is dead, and your biggest concern is swear words?"
"It wasn't a 'close call' for Serge."
entradas.menu: "It wasn't a 'close call' for Serge."

entradas.text: "I know. I still can't believe nobody was hurt."
entradas.menu: "I know. I still can't believe nobody was hurt."

entradas.text: "Language!"
entradas.menu: "Language!"

entradas.text: "You almost died *again*, and your biggest concern is swear words?"
"Mom would kill me for telling you this, but she was really worried."
"I know. I can't believe he's gone."
"Mom was inconsolable about it."
"How is your mother, anyway?"
entradas.menu: "How is your mother, anyway?"

entradas.text: "I was with Sheyna. We were, uh, studying."
He flung his backpack on the living room sofa and sprawled out in a chair.
"I hope you two are being careful."
entradas.menu: "I hope you two are being careful."

entradas.text: "So when's the wedding?"
entradas.menu: "So when's the wedding?"

entradas.text: "You *know* those brats? I was going to ask the guards to have them tear-gassed."
entradas.menu: "You *know* those brats? I was going to ask the guards to have them tear-gassed."

entradas.text: "You could've invited them in. There's enough food."
entradas.menu: "You could've invited them in. There's enough food."

entradas.text: "Ha. Even if they would cross the picket line, they're vegetarians."
"Don't do it. They brought goggles."
He flung his backpack on the living room sofa, sprawled out in a chair and sniffed the air.
"Nice. Mom never makes ribs at her new place."
Franc rolled his eyes.
"That's what Mom always says."
"How is Deana?"
entradas.menu: "How is Deana?"

entradas.text: Franc shrugged uncomfortably.
"She's fine, I guess. She's spending a lot of time volunteering with the Sordish League of Women."
"She won't tell me who she's voting for, except that it sure as hell isn't Lileas Graf."
"That's a relief."
entradas.menu: "That's a relief."

entradas.text: "Who are you voting for? Now that you're old enough."
entradas.menu: "Who are you voting for? Now that you're old enough."

entradas.text: "She won't tell me who she's voting for, but I think she's leaning PFJP."
"That's not surprising."
entradas.menu: "That's not surprising."

entradas.text: "Of course it does. Every vote counts."
"Jeez, Dad. Not everything is about you."
"I mean, I think between the divorce, Serge and Petr, she's been having a rough time."
"I mean, I think between the divorce and Petr, she's been having a rough time."
"I mean, I think between the divorce and Serge, she's been having a rough time."
"I mean, I think she's been taking the divorce pretty hard."
"And you haven't?"
entradas.menu: "And you haven't?"

entradas.text: "And I haven't?"
entradas.menu: "And I haven't?"

entradas.text: "It's different. I'm older."
"What about your mother?"
entradas.menu: "What about your mother?"

entradas.text: "Old enough to vote, even."
entradas.menu: "Old enough to vote, even."

entradas.text: "Does it matter?"
"Although it doesn't matter, does it?"
"No, I suppose not."
"Who will you vote for, Dad? Now that you're out of the running."
"I'd rather not say."
"Honestly, Lileas."
"Perhaps PFJP."
"Perhaps NFP."
Franc raised his eyebrows.
"Huh. Okay."
"Fair enough."
"Who would you vote for? I mean, if you weren't in the running."
"I'm voting for the candidate who...buys me a car?"
"Nice try, but no."
entradas.menu: "Nice try, but no."

entradas.text: "You want it, you got it."
entradas.menu: "You want it, you got it."

entradas.text: "Perhaps one of the small parties."
The oven timer went off. I took out the ribs and brought them to the dining room.
After we'd eaten, Franc kept toying with his fork. He looked preoccupied.
"What is it?"
entradas.menu: "What is it?"

entradas.text: "Was dinner all right?"
entradas.menu: "Was dinner all right?"

entradas.text: "Yeah, it was great."
Franc looked down at the tablecloth.
"Yes, I can see that."
entradas.menu: "Yes, I can see that."

entradas.text: "Dad, have you thought about quitting politics? I don't just mean dropping out of the race -- I mean retiring altogether."
"Dad, I think you should leave Sordland. It isn't safe here anymore."
"What gave you that idea? The bullets just barely whistling past my skull?"
entradas.menu: "What gave you that idea? The bullets just barely whistling past my skull?"

entradas.text: "That's ridiculous. I can take care of myself."
entradas.menu: "That's ridiculous. I can take care of myself."

entradas.text: "It's crossed my mind once or twice."
entradas.menu: "It's crossed my mind once or twice."

entradas.text: "Never."
entradas.menu: "Never."

entradas.text: "Are you insane, son?"
entradas.menu: "Are you insane, son?"

entradas.text: "It's just that... Deana told me she's getting bullied in school because of you. I've lost friends in the past months just for having the last name Rayne."
"Everything was so much easier before this. I think you were happier, too."
"I'm not talking about you."
"There's no guarantee that the same people who want you dead won't also come after Monica and Deana. Or me."
"That might have had something to do with it, yeah."
"No. I'm the target."
entradas.menu: "No. I'm the target."

entradas.text: "You might be right."
entradas.menu: "You might be right."

entradas.text: "You're watching too many conspiracy thrillers."
entradas.menu: "You're watching too many conspiracy thrillers."

entradas.text: "They killed Serge, didn't they?"
"They almost killed Serge, didn't they?"
"Haven't you thought about just laying low for a while?"
"I already said I'd retire. Isn't that enough?"
"And my politics professors said you don't have a chance of winning anyway."
"What? I'll show those eggheads!"
entradas.menu: "What? I'll show those eggheads!"

entradas.text: "I can't give up now, Franc. You're too young to understand."
entradas.menu: "I can't give up now, Franc. You're too young to understand."

entradas.text: "I didn't know how hard it was for you kids. I'm sorry."
entradas.menu: "I didn't know how hard it was for you kids. I'm sorry."

entradas.text: "Trust me, I understand."
"Just think about it. Please."
"I'd rather leave the country than admit defeat."
entradas.menu: "I'd rather leave the country than admit defeat."

entradas.text: "That's a little extreme. But sure, it might not hurt to lay low for a while."
"I'll do better going forward. I won't let you down."
entradas.menu: "I'll do better going forward. I won't let you down."

entradas.text: "You've made your point. I will."
entradas.menu: "You've made your point. I will."

entradas.text: "Isn't it enough that your mother and I are divorced?"
"I could go to Kyrute. It's the only truly neutral country on the continent."
entradas.menu: "I could go to Kyrute. It's the only truly neutral country on the continent."

entradas.text: "I don't know! Who knows what these people want?"
"Yes! Why not?"
"Just think about it. I'm serious."
"All right, Franc. I will."
entradas.menu: "All right, Franc. I will."

entradas.text: "You should go home, Franc."
entradas.menu: "You should go home, Franc."

entradas.text: "Stay and have a beer with me?"
entradas.menu: "Stay and have a beer with me?"

entradas.text: "No, I've got an exam tomorrow. Thanks for dinner, Dad."
"Yeah, I've got an exam tomorrow anyway. Thanks for dinner, Dad."
"Thanks, Dad. And thanks for dinner."
After showing Franc to the door, I sat and thought for a while.
"All right. Stay in denial."
"That's all I ask."
"You should go home, Franc. It's late."
entradas.menu: "You should go home, Franc. It's late."

entradas.text: "Stay and have a beer with me?"
entradas.menu: "Stay and have a beer with me?"

entradas.text: "Yeah, I've got an exam tomorrow anyway. Thanks for dinner, Dad."
"No, I've got an exam tomorrow. Thanks for dinner, Dad."
"And seriously, think about it."
"Dad, I can't keep coming over here."
"What? Why?"
entradas.menu: "What? Why?"

entradas.text: "Is it because of... how you got into Holsord State?"
entradas.menu: "Is it because of... how you got into Holsord State?"

entradas.text: "What has your mother been telling you about me?"
entradas.menu: "What has your mother been telling you about me?"

entradas.text: "Not to mention the way everyone's been treating me since they found out how I really got into Holsord State."
"Well, yeah."
"I've been the laughing stock of the school since the news came out."
"I worked so hard to prove I belonged there. I was actually getting good grades for the first time in my life! But now everyone thinks I'm just a daddy's boy."
"Would you rather have gone into the military?"
entradas.menu: "Would you rather have gone into the military?"

entradas.text: "Cry me a river. Your problems are nothing compared to mine."
entradas.menu: "Cry me a river. Your problems are nothing compared to mine."

entradas.text: "I'm sorry. I had no idea that would get leaked."
entradas.menu: "I'm sorry. I had no idea that would get leaked."

entradas.text: "Of course not."
"That makes this easier."
"I guess we both should have prepared for something like that."
"But I think I need to distance myself from you for a while. Until after the election, at least. Maybe longer."
"In any case, I think I need to distance myself from you for a while. Until after the election, at least. Maybe longer."
"I need to distance myself from you for a while. Until after the election, at least. Maybe longer."
"I need to show them I'm more than just Anton Rayne's son. And the more contact I have with you, the harder that will be."
"All right. I understand."
entradas.menu: "All right. I understand."

entradas.text: "Part of being your own man is not caring what other people think."
entradas.menu: "Part of being your own man is not caring what other people think."

entradas.text: "Great. So my whole family won't see me now."
entradas.menu: "Great. So my whole family won't see me now."

entradas.text: Franc shifted nervously in his seat.
"Well, Mom and Deana... you kind of brought that on yourself."
"Well..."
"I've been talking to Mom. About why she left."
"I've been the laughing stock of Holsord State since the news came out about how I got in."
Franc winced.
"Look, I don't know the full story."
"But if it's anything like what she said, it was bad."
"I didn't mean to hit her."
entradas.menu: "I didn't mean to hit her."

entradas.text: "Curtan Leste made me do it."
entradas.menu: "Curtan Leste made me do it."

entradas.text: "The Assembly members would've eaten her alive if I'd let her work with Ciara."
entradas.menu: "The Assembly members would've eaten her alive if I'd let her work with Ciara."

entradas.text: "I had to veto that bill. There were bigger forces at work."
entradas.menu: "I had to veto that bill. There were bigger forces at work."

entradas.text: "Come on, Dad. This was the one thing she wanted out of your presidency, and you took it away from her."
"I've been learning a lot about women's rights at university. I mean, I'm not one of those crazy 'male feminists', but I can sympathize."
"It's wrong that you always treated me so well while putting her down."
"Sordland is counting on me. I won't let the country down just because your classmates are calling you names."
entradas.menu: "Sordland is counting on me. I won't let the country down just because your classmates are calling you names."

entradas.text: "This was never about Sordland! It was only ever about you! God, Dad, can't you see that?"
"It doesn't matter what you meant!"
"Well, the thing with Mom... you kind of brought that on yourself."
"Franc, I know. I've been regretting it every day."
entradas.menu: "Franc, I know. I've been regretting it every day."

entradas.text: "I don't know if that's enough."
"Great. So my whole family hates me now."
entradas.menu: "Great. So my whole family hates me now."

entradas.text: "You're too young to understand."
entradas.menu: "You're too young to understand."

entradas.text: "Please, Franc. I've lost everyone else. I can't lose you too."
entradas.menu: "Please, Franc. I've lost everyone else. I can't lose you too."

entradas.text: "I don't hate you. I just need some space."
"That's bullshit. Listen, I just need some space."
"You're not losing me. I just need some space."
"Thanks, Dad."
"You've got that luxury. I don't."
"Good luck with the campaign."
"Good luck with retirement."
"You should go home, Franc. It's late."

entradas.text: "No, I've got an exam tomorrow. Thanks for dinner, Dad."

After showing Franc to the door, I sat and thought for a while.
My political career had taken so much away from me. My wife and daughter, and now my son...
And poor Serge...
Petr...
Where would it end?
I went up to my office and began drafting a speech announcing my decision to retire.
